UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user within the application, storing their profile information and assigned role for access control.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity.

displayName.description: The user's display name, typically obtained from the authentication provider.

role.description: The assigned role of the user (e.g., Admin, Editor, Viewer), dictating their permissions.

team.description: The discipline or team the user belongs to within the agency.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was last updated.

Quadrant.title: Quadrant
Quadrant.description: Defines a customizable category or axis on the Tech Radar, used for classifying items.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Quadrant entity.

name.description: The name of the quadrant (e.g., 'Tools & Platforms').

description.description: A brief description of what this quadrant represents.

order.description: A numerical value indicating the display order of the quadrant on the radar.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the quadrant was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the quadrant was last updated.

Ring.title: Ring
Ring.description: Defines a customizable adoption stage or concentric ring on the Tech Radar, indicating the maturity or recommendation status of an item.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Ring entity.

description.description: A brief description of what this ring's status implies.

order.description: A numerical value indicating the display order of the ring on the radar, typically from inner to outer.

color.description: A color code (e.g., hex) associated with the ring for visualization purposes.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the ring was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the ring was last updated.

Tag.title: Tag
Tag.description: Represents a keyword or category used to label and organize Radar Items for filtering and search.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Tag entity.

name.description: The name of the tag (e.g., 'AI', 'Cloud Computing').

description.description: A brief description of the tag's purpose or scope.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the tag was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the tag was last updated.

RadarItem.title: RadarItem
RadarItem.description: Represents a single tool, technique, or process placed on the Tech Radar.

id.description: Unique identifier for the RadarItem entity.

name.description: The official name of the radar item.

shortDescription.description: A brief summary of the radar item.

detailedNotes.description: Comprehensive notes and details about the radar item.

quadrantId.description: Reference to the Quadrant this item belongs to. (Relationship: Quadrant 1:N RadarItem)

ringId.description: Reference to the Ring this item belongs to. (Relationship: Ring 1:N RadarItem)

tagIds.description: References to Tags associated with this item. (Relationship: Tag N:N RadarItem)

ownerId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who is the primary owner or champion of this item. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N RadarItem)

team.description: The discipline or team primarily associated with this radar item.

maturityScore.description: A score (1-5) indicating the maturity level of the item.

impactScore.description: A score (1-5) indicating the potential impact of the item.

effortScore.description: A score (1-5) indicating the effort required to adopt or implement the item.

riskScore.description: A score (1-5) indicating the associated risk of the item.

costRange.description: The estimated cost range of the item (e.g., 'Free', 'Low', 'Medium', 'High').

links.description: An array of URLs providing additional documentation or vendor information for the item.

lastReviewedAt.description: The date and time when the item was last officially reviewed.

status.description: The current governance status of the item (e.g., 'Draft', 'In Review', 'Approved', 'Archived').

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the radar item was initially created.

createdBy.description: Reference to the UserProfile who created this item. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N RadarItem)

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the radar item was last updated.

updatedBy.description: Reference to the UserProfile who last updated this item. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N RadarItem)

ItemComment.title: ItemComment
ItemComment.description: Represents a comment made on a specific Radar Item, supporting discussions.

id.description: Unique identifier for the ItemComment entity.

radarItemId.description: Reference to the RadarItem the comment belongs to. (Relationship: RadarItem 1:N ItemComment)

parentId.description: Optional reference to a parent comment, enabling threaded discussions. (Relationship: ItemComment 1:N ItemComment)

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the comment was created.

createdBy.description: Reference to the UserProfile who created the comment. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N ItemComment)

ItemHistory.title: ItemHistory
ItemHistory.description: Records an audit trail of significant changes and actions performed on a Radar Item.

id.description: Unique identifier for the ItemHistory entity.

radarItemId.description: Reference to the RadarItem this history entry pertains to. (Relationship: RadarItem 1:N ItemHistory)

action.description: A description of the action performed (e.g., 'created', 'status_change', 'approved', 'ring_moved').

comment.description: An optional comment or justification for the action, especially for approval/rejection.

beforeValue.description: The state or value of a specific field before the action, if applicable.

afterValue.description: The state or value of a specific field after the action, if applicable.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the history event occurred.

createdBy.description: Reference to the UserProfile who performed the action. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N ItemHistory)

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed to adhere strictly to the core design principles, especially Authorization Independence and QAPs (Queries Are Not Filters), to ensure a secure, scalable, and debuggable system for the 'Agency Radar' application. 

**Authorization Independence:**
1.  **User Profiles:** User roles are stored directly within each user's profile document at `/userProfiles/{userId}`. This allows security rules to check `get(/userProfiles/$(request.auth.uid)).data.role` for role-based access control without complex lookups or dependencies, satisfying DBAC. The `userId` in the path directly corresponds to `request.auth.uid`, ensuring path-based ownership for profile management.
2.  **Radar Items:** Each `RadarItem` document in `/radarItems/{radarItemId}` contains all necessary authorization context: `ownerId`, `createdBy`, and `status`. Security rules can directly evaluate `resource.data.ownerId == request.auth.uid` or `resource.data.status == 'Approved'` without performing any `get()` operations on parent documents or other collections. This makes rules atomic, predictable, and robust against transactional complexities.
3.  **Item Comments & History (Denormalization for Subcollections):** To maintain strict Authorization Independence for subcollections, `ItemComment` and `ItemHistory` documents include denormalized fields from their parent `RadarItem`. Specifically, `radarItemStatus` and `radarItemCreatedBy` (representing the `status` and `createdBy` of the parent `RadarItem`) are copied into each `itemComment` and `itemHistory` document. This means that rules governing access to a comment or history entry can check its own fields (`resource.data.createdBy`, `resource.data.radarItemStatus`) without needing to fetch the parent `RadarItem` document. This is critical for simplifying security rules and enabling atomic writes to subcollections.

**QAPs (Queries Are Not Filters):**
1.  **Global Configuration Collections (`/quadrants`, `/rings`, `/tags`):** These collections are designed with a homogeneous security posture: read-only for all authenticated users and write-access for Admins. Since these are configuration data, full list reads are expected and efficient. Rules will simply allow `read` for authenticated users and `write` for Admins, ensuring no client-side filtering is required by the rules themselves.
2.  **Radar Items (`/radarItems/{radarItemId}`):** This collection handles various item states (Draft, In Review, Approved, Archived). Instead of segregating into separate collections, the `status` field is used as the primary mechanism for access control, alongside `createdBy` for ownership. 
    *   **Viewer Access:** Viewers can query `radarItems` where `status != 'Draft'`. The security rule will match this query exactly, allowing reads only for documents where `resource.data.status != 'Draft'`. This is a highly efficient and QAP-compliant query pattern. Editors/Admins will have broader read access.
    *   **Editor Access (Drafts):** Editors can list their own draft items by querying `radarItems` where `createdBy == request.auth.uid` AND `status == 'Draft'`. The rule will permit this read based on `resource.data.createdBy`, adhering to QAP.
3.  **Item Comments & History (`/radarItems/{radarItemId}/itemComments`, `/radarItems/{radarItemId}/itemHistory`):** Because the `radarItemStatus` and `radarItemCreatedBy` fields are denormalized into each comment/history document, security rules can evaluate read access for these subcollections directly based on their own document fields (e.g., `resource.data.radarItemStatus != 'Draft'`). This ensures that `list` operations on these subcollections for a given `radarItemId` are also QAP-compliant, as no `get()` calls to the parent `RadarItem` are needed to determine access rights for the comment/history entry itself.
